source_workstream.generator_model: configuration-model stub multiset; seeded Fisher-Yates shuffle; whole pairing discarded when loop or repeated undirected edge occurs; canonical edge sorting
source_workstream.prng: XorShift64*; deterministic pseudo-random only, not cryptographic
source_workstream.graph_identity: FNV-1a 64-bit over canonical ASCII DIMACS content (header plus sorted one-based edge lines); non-cryptographic checksum, not SHA-256
source_workstream.tie_seed_derivation: restart_seed = instance_seed XOR ((one_based_restart * 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15) modulo 2^64); restart uses same XorShift64* family and unbiased bounded sampling
source_workstream.implementation_boundary: Exploratory outcomes are from a transient independent JavaScript reference, never a Rust binary. Static review identified that the initial Rust candidate blob used a fresh stub clone per rejection and a different bounded-draw residue rule; the canonical Rust source has since been aligned to the JS seed-stream semantics. Graph-byte parity has not been run or established; regenerate and compare receipts once Rust tooling is available.

methodology.local_improvement: only for N <= 200; repeated feasible one-selected-for-two-compatible-nonadjacent exchange; max 2,000,000 candidate-pair checks; budget exhaustion recorded explicitly
methodology.outcomes: independence cardinality and ratio; local-search move counts; all outputs independently checked for feasibility; no wall-clock timing was collected

literature_target.title: A scalable quantum-enhanced greedy algorithm for maximum independent set problems on random regular graphs
literature_target.required_next_baseline: Marino-Kirkpatrick linear-time prioritized search under a documented faithful implementation
literature_target.note: This preflight compares only classical min-degree greedy, random tie-breaking, and small local improvement; it neither runs QGreedy nor reproduces the full paper.

claim_boundaries: Not a Rust execution or code validation.
Not the paper's QGreedy reproduction and no fixed QAOA angles or QAOA expectations were used.
The cohort is a small exploratory development pilot, not a pre-registered confirmatory set.
Best-of-16 consumes 16 runs per graph and must be compared at equal disclosed budget.
No runtimes were collected; no comparison can claim wall-clock or all-in-cost superiority.
No SOTA improvement or quantum advantage is claimed.
To reproduce graph bytes cryptographically, regenerate and record SHA-256 of the emitted DIMACS; the stored FNV values are only quick identity checks.

posthoc_uncertainty_analysis.analysis_unit: one graph instance; the 16 restart rows are nested within their graph and are not counted as 16 independent graph samples

overall.method: For each bootstrap replicate, resample graph instances with replacement separately within each N stratum, keep the original stratum sizes, then compute the instance-weighted mean objective delta. The percentile interval is post-hoc and does not account for choosing the portfolio after looking at results.

best_of_16_minus_single_deterministic_gr.cost_caveat: Best-of-16 uses 16 random-tie greedy trajectories against one deterministic greedy trajectory. This is not an equal-compute comparison and no timing was measured.

one_for_two_local_improvement_minus_sing.scope: N=50,100,200 only; no local-improvement result was run at N=500
one_for_two_local_improvement_minus_sing.method: Resample graph instances within each applicable N stratum, retaining stratum sizes; calculate one paired delta per graph.
one_for_two_local_improvement_minus_sing.interpretation: The one-for-two neighborhood gives small gains for some graphs and no gain for most. Its local-optimality certificate applies only to this neighborhood, not global MIS optimality.

caution: All values derive from an independent JavaScript preflight, not the Rust generator or runner.
Graph cohorts use newly derived seeds, not the authors' exact instances; this is not a graph-for-graph QGreedy reproduction.
These post-hoc summaries motivate fair resource-matched classical controls; they do not measure quantum advantage.
